LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the PKGBUILD and evaluates its top-level (global-scope) code. All executable logic in this PKGBUILD is contained inside function bodies: `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()`. The top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `source`, `sha256sums`, `validpgpkeys`) — no command substitutions, no downloads, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl` invocations, and no filesystem mutations. None of these top-level assignments execute external commands or produce side effects.

The `source` array defines a git source (`git+$url.git#tag=v$pkgver?signed`) and a local desktop file, with checksums set to `SKIP` for the VCS source and a concrete SHA-256 for the desktop file — these are recorded metadata only and are not downloaded or verified during `--printsrcinfo`. The `cargo fetch`, `pnpm install`, `cargo test`, and `install` commands live entirely within functions, which are not executed by this command.

No malicious or dangerous behavior is present in the global scope. The genuinely risky operations (such as `cargo fetch --locked`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and binary installation) are scoped to `prepare()`/`build()`/`package()` and therefore fall outside the scope of this specific `makepkg --printsrcinfo` gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments; no executable code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments; no executable code.
